    Dune Meadows: Multifactor Marginal Contrasts

    dune-marginal-contrasts.Rmd

    One-factor contrasts do not define how nuisance factors should be averaged. Phase 15 makes that choice explicit. This example tests management contrasts after adjusting for meadow use in a full-rank additive model.

    dune_factors <- data.frame(
  Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management),
  Use = droplevels(dune.env$Use)
)
dune_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management + Use,
  dune_factors,
  vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)

    derive_marginal_means() returns coefficient-space rows rather than inventing a response-space centroid. Equal weighting averages every level of Use equally. Proportional weighting uses the observed joint frequency of nuisance levels.

    equal_means <- derive_marginal_means(
  dune_design, "Management", weights = "equal"
)
proportional_means <- derive_marginal_means(
  dune_design, "Management", weights = "proportional"
)

equal_means$coefficient_rows
#>    (Intercept) ManagementHF ManagementNM ManagementSF         Use.L Use.Q
#> BF           1            0            0            0 -1.387779e-16     0
#> HF           1            1            0            0 -1.387779e-16     0
#> NM           1            0            1            0 -1.387779e-16     0
#> SF           1            0            0            1 -1.387779e-16     0
proportional_means$nuisance_weights
#> [1] 0.35 0.40 0.25

    The additive model makes pairwise management differences invariant to the Use weighting, although the marginal mean definitions themselves differ. In a full-rank interaction model the weighting can also change contrasts, so it is recorded in every result.

    planned <- rbind(
  `BF - HF` = c(BF = 1, HF = -1, NM = 0, SF = 0),
  `managed pair - other pair` =
    c(BF = 0.5, HF = 0.5, NM = -0.5, SF = -0.5)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_marginal_contrasts(
  dune_design,
  factor = "Management",
  contrasts = planned,
  weights = "equal",
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
planned_fit
#> Multifactor marginal distance contrasts
#> Target: Management  Weighting: equal 
#>                   contrast weighting df        ss denominator_df  pseudo_f
#>                    BF - HF     equal  1 0.1592432             14 0.9082249
#>  managed pair - other pair     equal  1 0.6524315             14 3.7210658
#>  p_perm p_adjusted adjustment
#>    0.45       0.45       holm
#>    0.02       0.04       holm
    pairwise_fit <- permanova_marginal_pairwise(
  dune_design,
  factor = "Management",
  weights = "proportional",
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
pairwise_fit
#> Multifactor marginal distance contrasts
#> Target: Management  Weighting: proportional 
#>  contrast    weighting df        ss denominator_df  pseudo_f p_perm p_adjusted
#>   BF - HF proportional  1 0.1592432             14 0.9082249  0.450      0.540
#>   BF - NM proportional  1 0.5898677             14 3.3642408  0.015      0.075
#>   BF - SF proportional  1 0.3549082             14 2.0241767  0.100      0.300
#>   HF - NM proportional  1 0.7186350             14 4.0986497  0.005      0.030
#>   HF - SF proportional  1 0.2308066             14 1.3163780  0.270      0.540
#>   NM - SF proportional  1 0.4130324             14 2.3556817  0.070      0.280
#>  adjustment
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm

    Each one-df hypothesis is a general linear contrast of the compiled model coefficients. Its reduced model retains every fitted direction orthogonal to that contrast, and its residuals receive a contrast-specific unrestricted Freedman–Lane permutation.

    Phase 15 rejects continuous nuisance variables, rank-deficient interaction grids, random effects, and implicit weighting. Those cases need an additional covariate-reference or mixed-denominator contract rather than a default guess.
